post.title: Nirvana Agent Sandboxes
post.hook: Pause an agent, delete its pod, keep its files. Resume from the last step.
post.summary: A one-pager and a bash script for creating managed agent sandboxes on Nirvana's NKS cloud through an OpenSandbox REST API. Covers an 11-call lifecycle API with optional persistent storage.
post.writeup:
## What it is
A reference kit for Nirvana's agent sandboxes: isolated, managed environments on NKS infra, built on AMD EPYC 9354P + DDR5 and OpenSandbox. The folder holds a one-page guide (`SANDBOX-ONE-PAGER.md`) and `create-sandbox.sh`, a script that creates a sandbox from the command line.

## Why it exists
Autonomous agents need somewhere safe to run code, and long jobs need to survive interruption. The kit documents how to get a sandbox quickly and how to park it without losing work.

## How it works
Two endpoints split the traffic. The API endpoint is the control plane (create, pause, resume, delete, diagnostics) and every call carries an `OPEN-SANDBOX-API-KEY` header. The gateway endpoint is the data plane, used to reach a port inside a sandbox by sending an `OpenSandbox-Ingress-To` routing header. A proxy route through the API server is the simpler, slower alternative.

Sandboxes are ephemeral by default (memory only, fastest start). With `extensions.persistence` set, a PVC mounts at `/workspace`. On pause the pod is deleted but the PVC stays; on resume a new pod re-mounts it, so an agent can pick up from its last checkpoint.

The script defaults to a `python:3.12-slim` image, 1 CPU, 1Gi memory, serving port 8000, and switches to a 50Gi persistent sandbox with `--persistent`. Everything is overridable by environment variable.

## Results
The one-pager lists 11 operations. Creation takes ~2.5s for ephemeral and ~6-7s for persistent sandboxes. Pause and delete are described as instant.

## Open questions
No benchmarks beyond the quoted creation times, and no tests. The script also needs a real API key to try. Storage class choice (`local-path` for dev, `abs` for prod) is left to the user.
